messages.subject: Is it appropriate to use scanone function directly on a genotype file from a RIL population ?
messages.subject_clean: Is it appropriate to use scanone function directly on a genotype file from a RIL population ?
messages.body_plain:
Could I just encode each SNP in my genotype file to (A,H,B) to
represent major homo, heterozygous, and minor homo?

I tried "ehk" and "imp" methods in R/qtl, and it looks fine, but I am
not sure it is an appropriate way or not, and whether the methods
specifically take the cross structure information into the analysis,
When I load that file by read.cross, it reports the data type is "F2"
cross.

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
> I think that will make r/qtl lose power to detect QTL. Is that right?

Not necessarily, but I'm assuming that your RIL lines are close to inbred and so there should be only a very small proportion of heterozygous genotypes.

> Actually, I want to find a general implementation of Haley-Knott
> regression and Imputation based regression from Sen and Churchill, are
> these two implementation in R/qtl are specifically designed for cross
> data?

Yes.

karl

messages.subject: variance accounted for by covariates in MQM
messages.subject_clean: variance accounted for by covariates in MQM
messages.body_plain:
I am building multiple QTL models for several traits and am including
covariate phenotypes for some traits. My question is what exactly the
variance attributed to the covariate represents in terms of potential
genetic variance attributable to both the trait being mapped and the
covariate. For instance, if mapping a phenotype with a strong
difference between sexes then one might expect that inclusion of sex
as a covariate will account (and thus remove) the effect of sex
determining loci in the model. Is this correct or are we in fact
potentially mapping sex determiners as well as QTL responsible for the
phenotype of interest?
Thanks
